analysis: The PR's only change is a one-line edit in the test helper at EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift:312, from `case .toolCall:` to `case .toolCall, .toolCallDelta:`. The patch shows no other changed lines. The helper's switch must now handle a new `.toolCallDelta` event case on `MLXServerGenerationEvent`, and the test simply ignores it. The supplied units (base lines 655-1818) are unchanged surrounding test code covering KV re-slice grants, paged pool shortfall telemetry, tool-choice enforcement, cacheSalt plumbing and local acquire routing. I found no production source change, no new attack surface, and no change to the controls in T-041 (cache scope, HMAC lookup, TTL), TB-007 or the tool-choice validation. The tests still assert fail-closed behavior for forced tool_choice, with no visible text before a validated call. Ignoring `.toolCallDelta` in the recording helper could mask a delta leak in those specific tests, but that is test-coverage hygiene, not a security regression. The production-side `.toolCallDelta` emission and its interaction with forced tool_choice validation (visible-text exposure before validation) are outside the supplied evidence. They should be checked wherever the event is introduced, in the main source files of this PR if any exist in other batches. No findings from these units.
